## How to read this

This measures **one human against the assistant on a sample**, not the quality of the labels in any absolute sense. It licenses a statement of the form "a human agreed with the assistant on N of M informative sampled judgements", and nothing stronger. It does not convert the remaining labels into human ones, and the scores built on them stay assistant-labelled.

A sample this size cannot detect a rare error. Treat a disagreement rate near zero as consistent with the labels being usable for a descriptive development result, not as evidence they are correct.
